repo.name: sitefetch
repo.description: Fetch an entire site and save it as a text file (to be used with AI models).

readme.summary: Well-structured README with excellent clarity and installation instructions, but lacks configuration details and troubleshooting guidance.
readme.top_issue: No troubleshooting section for common issues (rate limits, failed fetches, large sites, or CSS selector problems) and configuration options only reference external types.ts file without inline documentation

injection_risks.description: Potential for DOM-based XSS via user-controlled HTML content in the `toMarkdown` function
Use of `eval`-like functionality through `new Readability(window.document as any).parse()`

critical_findings: Potential for DOM-based XSS via user-controlled HTML content
security.summary: The sitefetch package has some security concerns, including potential injection risks and lack of input validation, but overall it appears to be a relatively secure package.

common_complaints: Code block formatting and content loss during extraction
Crashes and TypeErrors on certain websites
Out of memory issues with large websites
Unclear/missing documentation (output file location, match functionality)
Limited control over crawling scope (no single-page fetch option)
sentiment.summary: The sitefetch project shows signs of abandonment with numerous open critical bugs, zero maintainer engagement, and users expressing frustration with unresolved issues spanning 5+ months.

communication.summary: The responses are generally clear and helpful, showing a good level of patience with the maintainer.
